title: Client Reception Routine
summary: How to receive a client from arrival through a calm start to their visit.
relevance: The client reception routine sets the tone for the entire spa experience. For the team, it establishes a consistent, professional standard that reflects Zura Spa's values and ensures every client is handled with the same level of care. For the client, it creates a first impression of warmth, competence, and trust — making them feel welcomed, valued, and confident in their decision to visit.

items.label: Appearance
items.body: Clean, neat, and in full uniform. Hair should be tidy, nails trimmed, and personal hygiene impeccable.

items.label: Attitude
items.body: Calm, warm, and attentive. Avoid appearing rushed, distracted, or disinterested.

items.label: Disposition
items.body: Approachable and professional. Greet every client with a genuine smile and focused presence.

procedure.title: Stand
procedure.body: Rise to your feet as the client enters. Do not remain seated.

procedure.title: Greet
procedure.body: Offer a warm, professional welcome by name if known.

procedure.title: Offer a seat
procedure.body: Invite the client to sit comfortably.

procedure.title: Speak about services
procedure.body: Clearly present available services and answer any questions.

procedure.title: Confirm the service
procedure.body: Discuss and confirm the client's preferred service, massage needs, and payment method.

procedure.title: Optional mind game
procedure.body: Engage the client in a light, optional mind game before or after payment to ease any tension and enhance the experience.

procedure.title: Offer water
procedure.body: Offer water only after payment has been made and only upon request.

procedure.title: Alert therapists
procedure.body: Communicate all relevant details to the assigned therapist. Notify the assigned therapist(s) to prepare to receive the client. Wait for an affirmative response before proceeding.

procedure.title: Usher client upstairs
procedure.body: Escort the client to the massage room once the therapist confirms readiness.

notes.title: Things Not to Say During Client Reception
paragraphs: Avoid language, comments, or compliments that may:
list: Come across as overly familiar or inappropriate (e.g., personal remarks about a client's body or appearance)
Undermine confidence in the spa's services (e.g., expressing uncertainty about treatments)
Be dismissive or rushed (e.g., "It won't take long" or "We're almost done with someone else")
Involve sensitive topics such as religion, politics, or personal relationships
Include slang, informal language, or unprofessional humor
notes.closing: Always speak with intention. Every word during reception either builds or diminishes the client's trust.
